questions.q: A trader in Ibadan is treated for a stomach ulcer caused by Helicobacter pylori. The doctor prescribes a course of antibiotics. Why do the antibiotics help to control the ulcer?
options: They kill the bacteria in the stomach lining and reduce inflammation.
They neutralise the hydrochloric acid in the stomach.
They increase the secretion of mucus in the stomach.
They coat the ulcer surface to prevent food from irritating it.
questions.explanation: Antibiotics act against Helicobacter pylori, the bacterium that damages the stomach lining and causes inflammation; removing the bacterium allows the ulcer to heal. Neutralising acid or coating the ulcer may relieve symptoms, but these actions do not eliminate the bacterial cause.

questions.q: A village health worker in Sokoto plans to control guinea worm disease in a community that drinks from an open pond. Which measure would most directly prevent new infections?
options: Providing safe drinking water and filtering pond water before drinking.
Spraying the pond to kill adult mosquitoes.
Sleeping under insecticide-treated nets every night.
Vaccinating children against the guinea worm.
questions.explanation: Guinea worm is transmitted when people drink water containing infected copepods; filtering or using safe water breaks the transmission cycle. Mosquito control and sleeping under nets target malaria, and there is no routine vaccine against guinea worm disease.

questions.q: A patient in Enugu is diagnosed with sleeping sickness. Which organism is most directly responsible for transmitting the pathogen?
questions.explanation: Sleeping sickness is caused by trypanosomes and is transmitted mainly by the bite of the tsetse fly. Anopheles mosquitoes transmit malaria, while blackflies transmit onchocerciasis.

questions.q: When a person inhales, the diaphragm contracts and flattens. What is the immediate effect of this movement?
options: The thoracic cavity enlarges and air pressure inside it falls below atmospheric pressure.
The ribs move downward and inward, forcing air out of the lungs.
The thoracic cavity becomes smaller and air pressure inside it rises.
The glottis closes completely to trap air in the lungs.
questions.explanation: Contraction and flattening of the diaphragm increase the volume of the thoracic cavity, so the pressure inside falls and air is drawn into the lungs. The other described changes resemble exhalation or airway obstruction.

questions.q: A footballer in Lagos dislocates his shoulder during a match. Which structures normally hold the bones together at the shoulder joint and are most likely to be injured in this way?
questions.explanation: Ligaments are strong fibrous bands that connect bone to bone and stabilise joints such as the shoulder. Tendons attach muscle to bone, while cartilage reduces friction and synovial membranes secrete lubricating fluid.

questions.q: Which type of muscle is found in the wall of the human stomach and works without conscious control?
questions.explanation: The stomach wall contains smooth muscle, which contracts involuntarily to churn and move food. Cardiac muscle occurs only in the heart, and skeletal muscle is voluntary and attached to bones.

questions.q: A patient in Abuja has lymphatic vessels in one arm blocked after surgery. Which immediate change is most likely in that arm?
options: Digested food stops being absorbed from the small intestine.
Red blood cells are not formed in the bone marrow of that arm.
The blood loses its ability to clot.
Tissue fluid accumulates and causes swelling.
questions.explanation: Lymphatic vessels return excess tissue fluid to the blood; when they are blocked, fluid collects in the tissues and causes swelling known as oedema. Red blood cell formation, clotting and absorption from the small intestine are not directly prevented by blockage of lymph vessels in the arm.

questions.q: In the mammalian heart, which structure normally initiates each heartbeat by producing electrical impulses?
options: The atrioventricular valve in the right ventricle
The sinoatrial node in the right atrium
The bundle of His in the left ventricle
The semilunar valve in the aorta
questions.explanation: The sinoatrial node in the right atrium acts as the pacemaker and initiates the electrical impulse that spreads through the heart. The atrioventricular node and bundle of His conduct the impulse, but they do not normally set the resting rhythm.

questions.q: A mango farmer in Benue notices that sucrose made in mature leaves reaches the developing fruits. Through which tissue and process does this movement mainly occur?
questions.explanation: Sucrose is loaded into sieve tubes of the phloem and transported to sinks such as developing fruits by translocation. Xylem mainly transports water and mineral salts upward, and transpiration is the loss of water vapour rather than sugar transport.

questions.q: An adrenal cortex cell in a patient in Ibadan is specialised for secreting steroid hormones. Which organelle is expected to be especially abundant in this cell?
questions.explanation: Steroid hormones are lipids, and the smooth endoplasmic reticulum contains the enzymes for lipid and steroid synthesis. The rough endoplasmic reticulum mainly handles proteins, while the Golgi apparatus modifies and packages secretions.

questions.q: A student in Jos examines two adjacent living cells of a moss leaf. Which structure allows water and dissolved substances to pass directly between the cytoplasm of the two cells?
questions.explanation: Plasmodesmata are cytoplasmic channels that pass through the walls between adjacent plant cells. They allow water and dissolved substances to move directly from one living cell to another; stomata are openings to the air, and xylem vessels are dead water-conducting tubes.

questions.q: In a mesophyll cell from a mango leaf, where are the enzymes for the light-independent reactions of photosynthesis mainly located?
questions.explanation: The light-independent reactions, including the Calvin cycle, take place in the stroma of the chloroplast. The thylakoid membranes carry the light-dependent reactions, while the mitochondrial matrix is not the site of photosynthesis.

questions.q: Mr and Mrs Nwosu in Enugu have four daughters. What is the probability that their next child will be a boy?
questions.explanation: Each birth is an independent event, and the father contributes either an X-bearing or a Y-bearing sperm with equal probability. Therefore the chance of a boy is 1/2, regardless of the number of daughters already born.

questions.q: During protein synthesis, a mutation changes an mRNA codon from UGU, which codes for cysteine, to UGA, which is a stop codon. What is the most likely effect on the protein produced?
options: Protein synthesis stops early at that codon.
The reading frame shifts from that point onward
One amino acid is replaced by another without affecting length
The mutation has no effect on the protein
questions.explanation: UGA is a stop codon, so the ribosome is likely to terminate translation at that point, producing a shortened protein. A substitution changes one codon; it does not shift the reading frame as an insertion or deletion would.

questions.q: In a dihybrid cross AaBb × AaBb, the genes are on different chromosomes and show complete dominance. How many different phenotypes are expected among the offspring?
questions.explanation: With independent assortment and complete dominance, AaBb × AaBb gives four phenotype classes: both dominant, first dominant only, second dominant only, and both recessive. The expected ratio is 9:3:3:1, but only the number of phenotype classes is asked.

questions.q: A girl in Ibadan has a condition that reduces growth hormone secretion from the anterior pituitary. Which effect is most likely?
options: Increased reabsorption of water in the kidneys
Early onset of puberty due to excess oestrogen
Rapid rise in blood glucose after a meal
questions.explanation: Growth hormone from the anterior pituitary promotes growth, especially lengthening of bones. A deficiency during childhood therefore commonly causes stunted growth.

questions.q: Which division of the nervous system mainly controls involuntary activities such as heartbeat and movement of the gut?
questions.explanation: The autonomic nervous system controls involuntary effectors such as the heart, smooth muscle of the gut and glands. The somatic nervous system mainly controls voluntary skeletal muscles.

questions.q: A student in Abeokuta places four strips of onion epidermis in distilled water, 0.1 M sucrose, 0.3 M sucrose and 0.5 M sucrose solutions. After 20 minutes, in which liquid would the greatest number of cells be plasmolysed?
questions.explanation: The 0.5 M sucrose solution has the lowest water potential among the liquids, so onion cells lose the most water and many protoplasts pull away from the cell walls. Distilled water has the opposite effect, causing cells to take in water and become turgid.

questions.q: A student in Enugu places a crystal of potassium permanganate in a beaker of warm water and another crystal in a beaker of cold water. The purple colour spreads through the warm water faster. Which statement best explains the observation?
options: Active transport increases with temperature because the crystal supplies energy.
Diffusion is faster at higher temperature because the particles have more kinetic energy.
The crystal dissolves only in warm water, so the colour moves by gravity.
Osmosis is faster in warm water because the water particles are smaller.
questions.explanation: Potassium permanganate particles spread through the water by diffusion from where they are concentrated to where they are less concentrated. Warming increases the random movement of particles, so the purple colour spreads faster.

questions.q: A newly described insect from Calabar is given the scientific name Africalabus nigerensis. Which part of the name identifies the genus?
questions.explanation: In binomial nomenclature, the genus is the capitalized part of the scientific name. Thus Africalabus is the genus, while nigerensis is the specific epithet.

questions.q: A student in Ilorin finds an animal with a hard exoskeleton, two pairs of antennae and five pairs of walking legs. In which group of arthropods is it best classified?
questions.explanation: Two pairs of antennae are characteristic of crustaceans, and the hard exoskeleton places the animal among arthropods. Insects have one pair of antennae, arachnids have none, and myriapods have a different body and leg arrangement.

questions.q: A unicellular organism from pond water in Ogbomoso has no true nucleus, reproduces by binary fission and has a cell wall not made of cellulose or chitin. To which kingdom does it most likely belong?
questions.explanation: The absence of a true nucleus and reproduction by binary fission indicate a prokaryote, placed in the kingdom Monera. Its cell wall is also unlike the cellulose wall of plants or the chitinous wall of fungi.

questions.q: In a grassland near Minna, grass plants capture 50,000 kJ of energy from sunlight. If 10% of the energy is transferred from one trophic level to the next, how much energy is available to secondary consumers?
questions.explanation: Energy reaching primary consumers is 10% of 50,000 kJ = 5,000 kJ. Energy reaching secondary consumers is 10% of 5,000 kJ = 500 kJ, so 500 kJ is available to them.

questions.q: In a cocoa plantation near Ibadan, fallen leaves and cocoa pods are broken down by bacteria and fungi. Which statement best describes the role of these organisms in the carbon cycle?
options: They use sunlight to combine carbon dioxide and water into glucose.
They release carbon dioxide into the atmosphere through respiration as they decompose organic matter.
They convert nitrogen in the air into nitrates that the cocoa trees absorb.
They permanently lock carbon in dead matter so it cannot return to the atmosphere.
questions.explanation: Bacteria and fungi are decomposers; as they break down dead leaves and pods, they respire and release carbon dioxide. This returns carbon from dead organic matter to the atmosphere.

questions.q: An athlete in Abuja drinks about 1 litre of water after a race on a cool evening. Which change in the urine is most likely over the next two hours?
options: A larger volume of more dilute urine is produced.
A smaller volume of more concentrated urine is produced.
The same volume of urine is produced but with more urea.
No urine is produced because the extra water leaves only through sweat.
questions.explanation: Drinking a large amount of water lowers ADH secretion, so the kidney tubules reabsorb less water. The result is a larger volume of more dilute urine, especially on a cool evening when little water is lost by sweating.

questions.q: Birds can conserve water partly because their main nitrogenous excretory product is
questions.explanation: The main nitrogenous waste of birds is uric acid, which is relatively insoluble and is excreted as a semi-solid paste. This reduces the amount of water needed for excretion compared with urea or ammonia.

questions.q: Mr Bello, a poultry farmer in Ogun State, keeps only the hens that lay the most eggs for breeding over several generations. Which process is illustrated?
questions.explanation: Humans deliberately choose which individuals reproduce when a desired trait such as high egg production is selected, so the process is artificial selection. Natural selection depends mainly on environmental pressures, while mutation and genetic drift do not involve deliberate selection for egg number.

questions.q: Ngozi, a young child in Kaduna, has soft, bowed leg bones and poor growth. The doctor advises more sunlight and a diet rich in fish oil. Which nutrient is most directly deficient?
questions.explanation: Vitamin D is needed for calcium absorption and normal bone mineralisation, and its deficiency causes rickets with soft, bowed bones. Sunlight helps the skin make vitamin D, while fish oil is a good source. Vitamin C deficiency causes scurvy, iron deficiency causes anaemia, and thiamine deficiency causes beriberi.

questions.q: A public health officer in Enugu wants to reduce the spread of Lassa fever in a community where rats enter homes and food is often left uncovered. Which measure is most directly useful?
options: Storing food in rodent-proof containers and safely disposing of refuse
Sleeping under insecticide-treated nets every night
Boiling all drinking water before use
questions.explanation: Lassa virus spreads mainly through contact with food or household surfaces contaminated by infected rodent urine or faeces, so rodent control and safe food storage reduce transmission. Insecticide-treated nets target malaria mosquitoes, boiling drinking water mainly controls water-borne diseases, and antimalarial tablets do not prevent Lassa fever.

questions.q: A patient named Musa in Ibadan has a condition that prevents the diaphragm from contracting normally. Which immediate effect most directly reduces air entry into the lungs during inspiration?
options: The thoracic cavity cannot enlarge enough to lower the pressure around the lungs
Carbon dioxide cannot dissolve in blood plasma
Glucose cannot be broken down in body cells
Oxygen cannot combine with haemoglobin in the lungs
questions.explanation: During inspiration, contraction of the diaphragm increases the volume of the thoracic cavity and lowers the pressure around the lungs, so air is drawn in. If the diaphragm cannot contract, ventilation is reduced even before problems with gas transport or cellular respiration develop.

questions.q: A biology teacher in Ile-Ife records the ABO blood groups of students in a class. Which observation shows that blood group is an example of discontinuous variation?
options: Each student belongs to one of a few distinct blood groups with no intermediate types
The students' body masses vary gradually around an average
The students' heights form a smooth range from short to tall
The students' skin colours show many small gradations
questions.explanation: Discontinuous variation produces clear categories, such as the ABO blood groups, with no in-between values. Height, body mass and skin colour vary gradually and are examples of continuous variation.

questions.q: Tolu, a student in Ilorin, eats a meal containing beans. Which enzyme begins the breakdown of the bean protein in the stomach?
questions.explanation: Pepsin is a protease secreted in the stomach and activated by hydrochloric acid; it breaks proteins into peptides. Salivary amylase acts on starch, pancreatic lipase acts on fats, and maltase acts on maltose.

questions.q: Several pupils at a boarding house in Abeokuta have ringworm. Which practice is most directly useful in controlling its spread among them?
options: Avoiding the sharing of towels, combs and caps and treating infected pupils
Boiling all drinking water before use
questions.explanation: Ringworm is a fungal skin infection spread by direct contact or by sharing personal items such as towels and combs, so hygiene and prompt treatment reduce spread. Boiling drinking water, using insecticide-treated nets and measles vaccination target unrelated diseases.

questions.q: A catfish in a pond in Epe opens and closes its operculum rhythmically. Which feature of the gills makes oxygen uptake from water efficient?
options: The gills contain many air sacs that store oxygen
Water and blood flow in the same direction over the gill lamellae
The gill surface is dry and covered with a thick cuticle
Water and blood flow in opposite directions over the gill lamellae
questions.explanation: In counter-current flow, water and blood move in opposite directions across the gill lamellae, maintaining a diffusion gradient for oxygen along most of the gill. Same-direction flow quickly equalises oxygen levels, and fish gills must remain moist and thin for efficient gaseous exchange.

questions.q: The forelimbs of a whale, a bat and a human have similar sets of bones arranged in a similar order, although they are used for swimming, flying and grasping. This similarity is best explained as evidence of...
options: Homologous structures inherited from a common ancestor
Analogous structures produced by similar functions
Random differences with no evolutionary relationship
Structures changed by use and disuse during one lifetime
questions.explanation: Homologous structures share a basic anatomical plan because they were inherited from a common ancestor, even when their functions differ. Analogous structures perform similar functions but do not share the same basic structure, and changes acquired during one lifetime are not inherited in this way.

questions.q: A health worker in Ebonyi advises pregnant women to receive the required immunisation and to ensure clean cord care for their newborns. Which disease is this advice most directly intended to prevent?
questions.explanation: Neonatal tetanus occurs when tetanus spores enter through the unhealed umbilical stump, especially when cord care is unclean; immunising the mother protects the newborn. Measles and poliomyelitis are prevented by vaccines given to the child, while malaria is prevented mainly by mosquito control and other antimalarial measures.

questions.q: A young bean seedling in a school garden remains upright and flexible. Which tissue has unevenly thickened cellulose walls at the corners and gives mechanical support to the young stem?
questions.explanation: Collenchyma has unevenly thickened cellulose walls and living cells, giving flexible mechanical support to growing stems. Sclerenchyma is stronger but usually dead and rigid, while parenchyma is mainly for storage and turgor.

questions.q: The pectoral girdle of a human is attached to the axial skeleton less firmly than the pelvic girdle. What advantage does this give?
options: It allows the lower limbs to bear heavier loads.
It protects the abdominal organs more effectively.
It allows greater movement of the upper limbs.
It supports most of the body weight during standing.
questions.explanation: The loose attachment of the pectoral girdle permits a wide range of arm movements, which is useful for manipulation. The pelvic girdle, by contrast, is firmly joined to the vertebral column to transmit body weight.

questions.q: A dancer in Calabar bends one knee to lower her body. Which muscle group is the main flexor of the knee joint?
questions.explanation: Knee flexion is produced mainly by the hamstrings, which are the flexor muscles at the back of the thigh. The quadriceps group extends the knee, while the gastrocnemius mainly acts at the ankle and the gluteus maximus mainly extends the hip.

questions.q: In a healthy adult, most of the carbon dioxide from respiring tissues is transported in the blood as
options: lactic acid in red blood cells
questions.explanation: Most carbon dioxide is converted to hydrogencarbonate, which is carried mainly in the plasma. Smaller amounts are transported as carbaminohaemoglobin and as dissolved carbon dioxide, while lactic acid is not a main form of carbon dioxide transport.

questions.q: A trader in Onitsha notices that her legs swell when she stands for many hours. Which process normally removes excess tissue fluid and returns it to the blood?
options: Reabsorption by the loop of Henle
questions.explanation: Lymphatic vessels collect excess tissue fluid and return it to the venous blood, helping to prevent swelling. Blood capillary filtration tends to form tissue fluid, while the loop of Henle reabsorbs water in the kidney.

questions.q: A potted plant in Warri is watered heavily, but its roots become waterlogged and the plant wilts. Which statement best explains the wilting?
options: Root cells lack oxygen for respiration and absorb less water.
The xylem vessels become blocked by excess water and cannot carry sugar.
The roots take in too much water and burst.
Water moves from the soil into the leaves by active transport.
questions.explanation: Waterlogged soil has little air, so root cells cannot respire aerobically and active absorption of mineral ions and water is reduced, causing wilting despite abundant water. Xylem does not carry sugar, so the suggestion about blocked xylem and sugar is incorrect.

questions.q: Which pair of organelles is found in both a maize leaf cell and a human liver cell?
options: Cell wall and large central vacuole
questions.explanation: Mitochondria for respiration and ribosomes for protein synthesis occur in both plant and animal cells. Chloroplasts, a large central vacuole and a cellulose cell wall are features of the maize cell but not the liver cell.

questions.q: An onion epidermal peel is placed in a strong sugar solution. The cytoplasm and vacuole shrink away from the cell wall. What is this process called?
questions.explanation: In a strong sugar solution, water leaves the vacuole by osmosis, so the protoplast shrinks away from the wall; this is plasmolysis. Haemolysis and crenation refer to red blood cells, while turgidity is the firm state caused by water entry.

questions.q: In a dihybrid cross RrYy × RrYy, the genes are on different chromosomes and show complete dominance. What phenotypic ratio is expected in the offspring?
questions.explanation: Independent assortment gives four phenotypic classes in the ratio 9 dominant-dominant : 3 dominant-recessive : 3 recessive-dominant : 1 recessive-recessive. A 3:1 ratio is expected only for a single-gene heterozygous cross, and 1:1:1:1 is expected in a test cross with a double heterozygote and a double recessive.

questions.q: At the junction between two neurones, transmission of an impulse is normally one-way. Which statement best explains this?
options: The synapse contains a valve that opens only in the direction of the impulse.
Sodium ions move directly through fused membranes of the two neurones.
The myelin sheath allows impulses to cross only from the cell body to the axon.
Neurotransmitter is released from the presynaptic knob and binds to receptors on the postsynaptic membrane.
questions.explanation: An impulse crosses a synapse only when a neurotransmitter is released from the presynaptic knob and combines with receptor proteins on the postsynaptic membrane. This makes transmission unidirectional because the postsynaptic membrane does not release the same transmitter back across the gap. Direct flow of sodium ions through fused membranes is not how a typical chemical synapse works.

questions.q: A boy in Jos is suddenly frightened by a dog and runs away. Which response is directly caused by adrenaline released into his blood?
options: Peristalsis in the intestine increases and saliva secretion increases.
Blood vessels in the skin dilate and body temperature falls.
Liver glycogen is converted to glucose and the heart beats faster.
Blood glucose is lowered by increased uptake into muscle cells.
questions.explanation: Adrenaline prepares the body for 'fight or flight' by increasing heart rate and promoting the breakdown of liver glycogen to glucose. It does not increase intestinal peristalsis and salivation; those are associated with parasympathetic activity. It also does not lower blood glucose by increasing uptake into muscle cells.

questions.q: A man in Kano had a vasectomy two months ago. He still releases semen during ejaculation. Which statement best explains this?
options: The seminal vesicles and prostate gland still add their secretions to the semen.
Urine is added to the semen to replace sperm.
Sperm are still stored in the epididymis and are released during ejaculation.
The testes continue to release mature sperm directly into the urethra.
questions.explanation: After vasectomy, the vas deferens is cut, so sperm cannot enter the semen, but the seminal vesicles and prostate gland still secrete the fluid part of semen. Therefore ejaculation can still occur although the semen contains no sperm. Sperm are not released directly from the testes into the urethra.

questions.q: A freshwater fish in a Lagos aquarium needs to take up certain salts from water even when their concentration in the water is lower than in its blood. Which process enables this uptake?
options: Osmosis down a water potential gradient.
Simple diffusion along a concentration gradient.
Filtration caused by pressure from the heart.
Active transport using energy from respiration.
questions.explanation: The fish absorbs salts against their concentration gradient, which requires energy supplied by respiration; this is active transport. Osmosis and simple diffusion only move substances down their gradients, and filtration is mainly pressure-driven.

questions.q: A patient in Ibadan suffers damage to the medulla oblongata after a road accident. Which function is most directly affected?
options: Interpretation of visual images from the eyes.
Control of learned speech and memory.
Regulation of breathing and heart rate.
Coordination of balance and voluntary movement.
questions.explanation: The medulla oblongata controls involuntary activities such as breathing, heart rate and blood pressure. Damage there most directly disturbs these vital autonomic functions. Balance and voluntary movement are coordinated by the cerebellum, while visual interpretation and speech involve the cerebrum.

questions.q: In a human male, the testes are located in the scrotum outside the abdominal cavity mainly because
options: sperm need space to mature into eggs.
the slightly lower temperature is necessary for normal sperm production.
the testes are unable to respond to hormones inside the abdomen.
it protects sperm from high blood pressure in the abdomen.
questions.explanation: Sperm production in mammals requires a temperature slightly lower than normal body temperature, which is provided by the scrotum. The scrotum is not for producing eggs, and sperm are not protected from abdominal blood pressure by being outside the abdomen.

questions.q: Some dry raisins were placed in distilled water. After two hours they became swollen. Which explanation is correct?
options: The raisins lost solutes to the water and became turgid.
Water entered the raisins by osmosis because their cells contained a more concentrated solution.
Sugar moved out of the raisins by diffusion, causing water to follow.
Water was pumped into the raisins by active transport against a gradient.
questions.explanation: The raisin cells contain concentrated sugar solution, so their water potential is lower than that of distilled water. Water therefore enters the cells through the semi-permeable membrane by osmosis and the raisins become swollen and turgid. Sugar does not move out to pull water in; osmosis is the net movement of water down a water potential gradient.

questions.q: In the hierarchy of biological classification, which rank contains the greatest number of different organisms?
questions.explanation: In the taxonomic hierarchy, a kingdom is a broad group made up of many phyla, classes, orders, families, genera and species. Species is the smallest and most specific rank among the listed groups. Hence kingdom contains the greatest number of different organisms.

questions.q: Which change in a boy at puberty is directly stimulated by testosterone?
options: Widening of the hips and onset of menstruation.
Deepening of the voice and growth of facial hair.
Development of mammary glands and a high-pitched voice.
Early closure of the epiphyseal plates and loss of body hair.
questions.explanation: Testosterone is the main male sex hormone and stimulates male secondary sexual characteristics such as deepening of the voice and growth of facial and body hair. It does not cause menstruation, widening of hips, or development of mammary glands, which are associated with female hormones.

questions.q: A student in Jos observes a microscopic organism with a nucleus, no cell wall and movement by pseudopodia. In the five-kingdom system, it is best placed in
questions.explanation: Amoeba is a unicellular organism with a true nucleus, no cell wall and pseudopodia for movement; in the five-kingdom system it is classified under Protista. Monera are prokaryotic, while Fungi have cell walls and Plantae contain photosynthetic multicellular organisms.

questions.q: Runoff from a farm near Epe carrying nitrates and phosphates enters a slow-flowing pond. Which sequence best explains why many fish in the pond may later die?
options: Algae grow rapidly, then decay; decomposition uses up dissolved oxygen and fish suffocate.
The runoff raises the water temperature so much that fish cannot obtain oxygen.
Algae absorb all the minerals, so fish die from lack of minerals in the water.
The nitrates and phosphates directly poison fish by stopping gill movement.
questions.explanation: The added nutrients cause an algal bloom. When the algae die, bacteria decompose them and use dissolved oxygen, so oxygen falls below the level needed by fish. Direct poisoning and mineral removal are not the main cause.

questions.q: In a pond near Lokoja, phytoplankton contain 40,000 kJ of energy. If 10% of the energy is transferred at each trophic level, how much energy is available to small fish that feed on zooplankton that feed on phytoplankton?
questions.explanation: Energy available to zooplankton = 40,000 × 10/100 = 4,000 kJ. Energy passed to small fish = 4,000 × 10/100 = 400 kJ. The value 4,000 kJ is only the energy at the zooplankton level.

questions.q: At a hospital in Zaria, blood in the renal artery of a healthy patient is found to contain more urea than blood in the renal vein. Which explanation is best?
options: The renal vein carries urine directly from the kidney to the bladder.
The kidney removes urea from the blood and passes it into urine, so less urea leaves in the renal vein.
The kidney converts urea in the renal artery into glucose for the blood.
The renal artery contains more water from filtration, which dilutes the urea in the renal vein.
questions.explanation: The kidney filters and secretes urea into the tubules, and it is excreted in urine. Blood leaving through the renal vein therefore has a lower urea concentration than blood entering through the renal artery. The vein does not carry urine; urine leaves through the ureter.

questions.q: A man in Ilorin trains with weights for many years and develops very large muscles. His children, however, are not born with particularly large muscles. Which statement best explains this?
options: Large muscles are a recessive trait that disappears in the next generation.
Changes in body cells during his lifetime do not alter the genes carried in his gametes.
The environment cannot affect the phenotype of the man's muscles.
The children would develop large muscles only if they also received a mutation from him.
questions.explanation: Only inherited changes in genes in gametes can be passed to offspring. Training enlarges muscles through environmental effects on body cells, not by changing the genetic information in sperm cells, so the acquired characteristic is not inherited. This is the basis of rejecting Lamarckian inheritance for such traits.

questions.q: A pupil in Ilesa has bleeding gums, loose teeth and wounds that heal slowly. Which vitamin deficiency is most likely?
questions.explanation: Vitamin C is needed for collagen formation, which strengthens gums, teeth and healing tissues; deficiency causes scurvy. Vitamin K is mainly involved in blood clotting, while vitamins A and D have other roles.
